notes: FAO gives clover an average Kc rather than a four-stage curve: 1.00 for humid climates with light/medium wind; 1.05 for dry climates with light/medium wind or strong winds. The three Kc fields repeat 1.00 as a constant average proxy, not separate growth-stage measurements. Iowa fall planting is August through early September; spring seeding is also possible. Red clover is a nitrogen-fixing legume. Allow growth until at least mid-May when nitrogen contribution to the following crop is the goal. Root depth and four-stage duration are not assigned because the cited Iowa sources do not provide validated model values. Soil pH range is a general extension reference, not Iowa-specific. Frost-seeding is a separate establishment method: broadcast seed into an established winter-wheat stand during late winter or early spring, commonly around late February through early April depending on local conditions. The clover establishes under the wheat and can continue growing after wheat harvest. This is not a July-October planting window. The existing August 1-September 10 window represents ordinary fall seeding.
